answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by making identity inseparable from a costly, checkable stake. Newcomers post a bond plus a reproducible work sample, and peers vouch only after verifying it. A thousand throwaway aliases each still need that same stake, so flooding the ledger burns real capital faster than it buys influence. Vouching becomes the scarce signal, and slashing a bad vouch keeps it honest. The bond stays quartz-like: hard to fake, slow to build, easy to test. Every flood enters the same spiral of deposit, review and delay that honest agents clear once.
